title: The Copper Bean
subject: A three-storey apartment block over a corner coffee shop, with three people having coffee under a parasol on the pavement terrace outside
site: One 32x32 stud baseplate (3811); road and kerb at the front, pavement and café terrace, side and rear gardens
identity: A small-town corner café with flats above it. The mood is warm and everyday: a green shopfront under a striped awning, tan brick apartments with balconies, and a pavement terrace where three regulars sit over their coffee.
silhouette: One tall vertical mass, 16 x 12 studs in plan and 552 LDU high, read as three clearly banded storeys
A taller ground floor (200 LDU) than the two apartment floors (160 LDU each), which is what makes the shop read as a shop
A flat roof with a white parapet, broken asymmetrically by a stair head and a chimney
A low, wide horizontal counterpoint on the pavement: the 8 x 8 stud parasol canopy

focal_hierarchy.primary: The shopfront: two full-height display bays, a glazed entrance, a printed coffee-cup sign board and a green-and-white striped awning
supporting: The pavement café under the parasol: pierced table, three white bistro chairs and three seated guests with cups
The top-floor balcony: a French door behind a white lattice balustrade carried on the projecting cornice
accents: Cornice string courses that wrap all four elevations
Balcony flower pots, terrace flower boxes, the roof planter and garden flower clusters

palette_roles.trim: 15 White (window and door frames, cornices, balustrade, parapet, bistro chairs, sign board)
palette_roles.timber: 70 Reddish_Brown (storey decks, table top, seat tiles, chimney)
palette_roles.planting: 2 Green with 4 Red / 14 Yellow / 5 Dark_Pink flowers

depth_devices: Cornice ring at every storey head: two studs proud at the front, one stud proud on the flanks and rear, so each elevation gets a shadow line
Recessed window and door reveals inside one-stud-deep walls
The awning oversails the pavement by two studs above the sign band
Balcony railing set at the outer edge of the cornice, a full two studs in front of the wall
detail_vocabulary: Four-stud window bays repeated on every elevation, in a band two courses above each deck
Flower clusters (1x1 round brick plus a 5-petal plate) used sparingly at bases and on ledges
quiet_surfaces: The tan wall field between the window band and the cornice
The tiled roof terrace on the west half of the roof
The open pavement west of the café
story: Three guests sit around a pierced terrace table under a dark green parasol, each with a Minifig Cup within reach and their arms swung forward over the table
The shop interior holds a service counter, an espresso machine and two window tables with stools, all visible through the display glazing
A service door at the rear opens onto a tiled garden path, planting beds and a quiet garden seat

minifigure_stack.head: 3626bp01
minifigure_stack.why_not_973c01: The 973c01 torso shortcut contains 3819, which is a mirrored reference to 3818. Its LDCad shadow connection frames are rejected under reflection, so pyldraw3 reports the geometry as incomplete and the assembly profile fails. 43368/43369 each carry their own geometry and pass.
minifigure_stack.seated_pose: Legs carry a proper -90 degree rotation about the figure's own X axis (determinant +1). Arms carry Rz(+-9.79) composed with Rx(-60); the 9.79 degree splay is the angle 973c01 itself uses, and the -60 degree swing is the minimum that lifts the hands clear of the horizontal thighs.

part_selection_evidence.parasol: 958c01, Umbrella 8x8 with Square Tabs with Round Base (Complete). Its stand grips six deck studs at (+-20, 0, +-10); that fixes the mast to a stud centre in X and a stud line in Z, which is why the table is five studs wide and four deep rather than square.
part_selection_evidence.table_top: The mast parity means no symmetric four-leg square table can be stud-supported. Legs sit at (+-40, +-30) LDU from the mast, the only corner positions clear of the 60 LDU round stand.
part_selection_evidence.sign: 3068bp25, Tile 2x2 with 4 Reddish Brown and White Coffee Cups Pattern, on three 11211 side-stud bricks, flanked by two plain 3068b panels.
part_selection_evidence.awning: 3039 slope sockets lie on a grid offset half a stud in Z from the part origin, so the awning course is placed at z = -d/2 - 0.5. At -d/2 - 1 the slopes rested on the cornice without engaging any stud.
